investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: upstream model provider returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, blocking all required evidence collection
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency error with error code provider_account_unavailable. Because the LLM call never completed, the probe received no response payload and therefore collected zero of the five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), causing a total contract validation failure. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the model provider connectivity layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the configured model provider at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T13:04:11–13:04:17Z). The runtime test endpoint surfaced this as a 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable, which the harness translated into a 502 bad_gateway response. Because the LLM call failed before producing any output, the probe returned an empty evidence object, violating all five fields required by the local-agent-runtime expected-output contract. The failure is isolated to the runtime/test call path; sibling checks local-agent-create and local-agent-permissions, which do not invoke the LLM, both passed in the same run.

possibleCauses: Primary: Transient model provider outage or degradation at the time of the eval run, causing the AURA backend to return 424 provider_account_unavailable for all LLM inference requests routed through the runtime/test endpoint.

Secondary: A provider account credential, quota, or routing configuration issue on the AURA backend side that caused the provider to be unreachable specifically for the eval harness account or org, while not affecting agent creation or permissions endpoints.

Tertiary: A backend-side regression in the runtime/test endpoint's provider routing or dependency resolution that causes it to fail with 424 under certain conditions — this is a hypothesis only, as sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty and no supporting source evidence links a code change to this endpoint's behavior.

investigation.title: Project Agent Chat Stream Eval Failure: HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable Blocks Session Persistence and Text Generation
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-chat-stream failed because the AURA backend returned HTTP 424 (Failed Dependency) with error code provider_account_unavailable during the chat stream turn, preventing the agent from generating any text output or persisting a session. As a direct consequence, the three session-dependent evidence fields (sessionId, sessionCount, expectedPhrase) were never produced, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unreachable from AURA's backend at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T13:04:23Z). The API returned HTTP 424 with code provider_account_unavailable and support_id aaa6c194bd35, terminating the chat stream before any text_delta frames, session persistence, or phrase generation could occur. This is an eval-time infrastructure signal, not a confirmed user-facing production outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: HTTP 424 response with code provider_account_unavailable and support_id aaa6c194bd35 was returned during the project-agent-chat-stream probe run.
failed-check.evidence: frameTypes array contains 'error' and 'message' frames but no 'text_delta' frame; textSample is empty string, confirming no model output was produced.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase are all absent from the collected evidence, consistent with the stream being terminated before session creation or text generation.

sibling.session-share-public-read: The session-share-public-read sibling check received the identical HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable error (support_id 0fc8c25201ba), confirming the provider unavailability affected at least two independent chat-stream-dependent checks in the same run window.

sibling.project-agent-tool-roundtrip: frameTypes also contains 'error' with no tool invocations (toolNames=[]), textSample empty, consistent with the same provider failure cutting off the stream before tool use.

sibling.project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: sessionSubagentError states 'Parent chat stream did not emit a child run id', and taskToolUsed=false, subagentSpawned=false — all consistent with the stream being terminated by the provider error before any agent work began.

sibling.project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: reviewerEventsError is 'Timed out after 120000ms waiting for expected value'; reviewerEventCount=0; toolNames=[]; listAgentsUsed=false — consistent with the planner agent stream also being cut off by the provider error.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:114-122: The contract at line 120 requires sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase; none were present in the collected evidence.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=8598, well below the warningLatencyMs=30000 threshold, indicating the probe did not time out but received an early error response.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] AURA's backend model provider integration was transiently unavailable at the time of the eval run, causing HTTP 424 to be returned for all chat stream requests. Both project-agent-chat-stream (support_id aaa6c194bd35) and session-share-public-read (support_id 0fc8c25201ba) received this error within the same run window, indicating a provider-side or AURA-side routing issue affecting all model-dependent agent operations.

[Medium confidence] A transient network or authentication fault between AURA's backend and the model provider caused the dependency failure. The error message explicitly states 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits', pointing to AURA infrastructure rather than eval credentials.

[Lower confidence] The eval probe's access token or project/agent configuration was valid (orgId, projectId, agentId, agentInstanceId were all present and non-empty) but the downstream model call failed, ruling out eval credential misconfiguration as the primary cause.

The stream emitted an "error" frame instead of tool-use frames, so toolNames remained empty and every downstream tool-execution assertion failed. investigations.title: harness-skill-invocation eval fail: installed skill not surfaced in context and probe phrase absent from chat response
investigations.summary: The harness-skill-invocation eval completed a full chat turn (latencyMs=11002) but the agent's response was empty (textSample="") and neither contained the expected phrase "AURA_SKILL_PROBE_OK" nor showed the installed skill in context (skillInContext=false, textMatches=false). Skill creation and installation both succeeded (created=true, installedOnAgent=true), isolating the failure to the chat-turn execution layer rather than the skill management APIs.
investigations.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but the evidence localizes it to the chat-turn execution path inside runSkillInvocationTurn (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1670). The agent session produced an "error" frame during the turn (frameTypes includes "error"), the response text was empty (textSample=""), and the skill was not injected into the model context (skillInContext=false, skillLabels=[]). This indicates the chat stream either errored before the skill context was assembled and delivered to the model, or the skill context injection step silently failed, preventing the model from ever seeing the skill and producing the probe phrase. No shared-dependency failure is indicated because both sibling checks harness-memory-roundtrip and harness-skills-roundtrip passed in the same run window.
proof: failed-check.message: 'textMatches expected true but got false; skillInContext expected true but got false' — the two contract assertions that failed are the ones gating skill context delivery and model response content.
failed-check.evidence: textSample is empty string, skillLabels is empty array, skillInContext=false — the model received no skill context and produced no output text.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes includes 'error' alongside 'assistant_message_start' and 'message' — an error frame was emitted during the chat stream, consistent with a mid-stream failure before or during skill context injection.
failed-check.evidence: created=true and installedOnAgent=true — skill creation and installation APIs succeeded; the failure is downstream of those steps, in the chat-turn path.
sibling.harness-skills-roundtrip: status=pass, agentContainsSkill=true — the skill management roundtrip (create/install/delete) passed in the same run, confirming skill CRUD APIs are healthy.

expected-output.contract: assertions require textMatches=true, skillInContext=true, and expectedPhrase='AURA_SKILL_PROBE_OK' — all three are tied to the model having received and acted on the skill during the chat turn.

possibleCauses: Skill context injection failure during chat-turn setup: the installed skill was not assembled into the model context before the turn was dispatched, resulting in skillInContext=false and an empty or error response. This is the strongest hypothesis given skillInContext=false and skillLabels=[] despite installedOnAgent=true.

Chat stream error interrupting the turn before the model could respond: the 'error' frame in frameTypes suggests the stream encountered a runtime error mid-turn, which may have caused the response to be discarded or truncated to empty, consistent with a chat stream interruption recovery scenario.

Skill context assembly returning empty labels: skillLabels=[] despite the skill being installed suggests the context-building step either did not query the installed skills for this agent instance or the query returned no results, possibly due to a timing or scoping issue between skill installation and context assembly.

Agent instance scoping mismatch: the skill was installed on the agent (agentId) but the chat turn may have used an agent instance (agentInstanceId) that did not inherit or resolve the installed skill list at turn time.

Transient runtime error in the desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 environment: the error frame could reflect a one-time harness or network fault; no run history is available (previousRunCount=0) to distinguish a regression from a transient failure.

investigations.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: upstream model provider returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, blocking all required evidence collection
investigations.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency error with error code provider_account_unavailable. Because the LLM call never completed, the probe received no response payload and therefore collected zero of the five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), causing a total contract validation failure. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the model provider connectivity layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the configured model provider at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T13:04:11–13:04:17Z). The runtime test endpoint surfaced this as a 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable, which the harness translated into a 502 bad_gateway response. Because the LLM call failed before producing any output, the probe returned an empty evidence object, violating all five fields required by the local-agent-runtime expected-output contract. The failure is isolated to the runtime/test call path; sibling checks local-agent-create and local-agent-permissions, which do not invoke the LLM, both passed in the same run.

investigations.summary: The `project-agent-a2a-roundtrip` eval on `desktop-release` (desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64) failed because the planner agent never invoked `list_agents` or `send_to_agent`—`toolNames` is empty, `listAgentsUsed` and `sendToAgentUsed` are both false, and the reviewer agent received zero events before timing out after 120 000 ms (evidence: `failed-check.message`, `failed-check.evidence`). investigations.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but the strongest hypothesis is a transient model-provider outage during the eval window (2026-10-02T13:04:31Z–13:07:25Z). Because the model never produced a tool-call response, the planner could not call `list_agents` or `send_to_agent`, making the entire A2A roundtrip impossible regardless of routing or A2A infrastructure correctness. The API returned HTTP 424 with code provider_account_unavailable and support_id aaa6c194bd35, terminating the chat stream before any text_delta frames, session persistence, or phrase generation could occur.
